summary: Some korbanos chatas are left to die, like the baby of a chatas or a chatas whose owner died. A lost chatas that was found with a blemish is treated one way if the owner already got his kapparah, and another way if he did not.
stIntro: This mishna, which also appears in tractate Temura, deals with the five sin offerings left to die. It is cited here because of its relevance to the halakhot of misuse. The mishna first mentions three of those offerings:

chunks.en: The baby of a chatas, and the temurah of a chatas,
chunks.st: The offspring of a sin offering, and an animal that is the substitute for a sin offering,
chunks.stMore: whether or not the owners achieved atonement by means of another offering,

words.note: A korban brought for doing an aveirah by mistake.
An animal someone tried to swap for a korban; it becomes holy too.

chunks.en: and a chatas whose owner died, must die.
chunks.explain: They are left alone until they die.
chunks.st: and a sin offering whose owners have died before the offering was sacrificed, shall die.

chunks.en: One whose year passed,
chunks.st: And the other two sin offerings left to die are the sin offering whose year since birth passed
chunks.stMore: and is therefore unfit for sacrifice,

chunks.en: or that got lost and was found with a blemish,
chunks.st: and a sin offering that was lost and when it was found it was blemished,
chunks.stMore: with regard to which the halakhot are as follows:

chunks.en: if the owner already got his kapparah,
chunks.st: If the sin offering was found after the owner achieved atonement through the sacrifice of another animal as a sin offering,

chunks.en: it must die, and it does not make a temurah,
chunks.st: then the blemished animal shall die, and it does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute,
chunks.stMore: as it is has neither inherent sanctity, which would make it fit for sacrifice on the altar, nor sanctity that inheres in its value.

chunks.en: and one may not benefit from it,
chunks.st: And one may not derive benefit from the found animal ab initio,

chunks.en: but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: but if he derived benefit from the animal he is not liable for its misuse.

words.note: Me'ilah is using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for yourself.

chunks.en: And if the owner did not yet get his kapparah,
chunks.st: And if the animal whose year passed was found before the owner achieved atonement,

chunks.en: it grazes until it gets a blemish,
chunks.st: the found animal shall graze until it becomes blemished [shetista’ev], at which point it may not be sacrificed;

chunks.en: and it is sold, and he brings another one with its money,
chunks.st: and it shall be sold and the owner shall purchase another animal with the money received from its sale.
chunks.stMore: The animal that was found blemished may be sold immediately, and the owner shall purchase another animal with the money received from its sale.

chunks.en: and it makes a temurah,
chunks.st: In both cases, the animal renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute,

chunks.en: and it has me'ilah.
chunks.st: and one who derives benefit from it is liable for misusing it.

summary: A nazir set aside money for his korbanos without saying which money is for which korban. There is no me'ilah, since all of it could be used for a shelamim. The mishnah teaches what happens to the money if he dies.

chunks.en: Someone who set aside money for his korbanos of nezirus,
chunks.st: In the case of a nazirite who designated money for the three offerings he is obligated to bring upon completion of his naziriteship,
chunks.stMore: a sin offering, a burnt offering, and a peace offering, but he did not specify which money was designated for which offering,

words.note: A nazir promises not to drink wine or cut his hair; at the end he brings korbanos.

chunks.en: may not benefit from it, but there is no me'ilah,
chunks.st: since it is not clear what the money is intended for, one may not derive benefit from the money ab initio, but if he derived benefit from the money he is not liable for its misuse.

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן רְאוּיִין לָבֹא כֻלָּן שְׁלָמִים.
chunks.en: because all of it could be used for shelamim.
chunks.st: This is due to the fact that all the money is fit for purchase of the peace offering,
chunks.stMore: for which one is liable for misuse only after its blood is sprinkled, and therefore there is no liability for its misuse.

words.note: Peace offerings, shared by the mizbeach, the Kohanim and the owners.

chunks.en: If he died and the money was not specified,
chunks.st: If the nazirite died and he had undesignated funds,
chunks.stMore: meaning he did not specify which money was for each of the three offerings,

chunks.en: it goes for nedavah korbanos.
chunks.st: all the money will be allocated for purchase of communal gift offerings.

words.note: Korbanos given as a gift, by choice.

chunks.en: If the money was specified,
chunks.st: If the nazirite died and he had specified money,

chunks.en: the money for the chatas goes to the Dead Sea,
chunks.st: the money specified for purchase of the sin offering shall go to the Dead Sea
chunks.stMore: for disposal,

words.note: The Dead Sea.

chunks.en: one may not benefit from it, but there is no me'ilah with it.
chunks.st: because one may not derive benefit ab initio from the money of a sin offering whose owner has died. But if it was not disposed of, and one derived benefit from the money, he is not liable for its misuse.

chunks.en: The money for the olah,
chunks.st: With the money specified for purchase of the burnt offering,

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: they bring an olah, and it has me'ilah.
chunks.st: one shall bring a gift burnt offering, and one is liable for misusing the funds.

chunks.en: And the money for the shelamim,
chunks.st: With the money specified for purchase of the peace offering,

chunks.en: they bring shelamim,
chunks.st: one shall bring a gift peace offering.
chunks.stMore: Although it is a gift offering, the restrictions of the peace offering of the naziriteship apply,

chunks.en: and it is eaten for one day,
chunks.st: and therefore it is eaten for one day
chunks.stMore: and that same night, not the standard two days and one night of a regular peace offering.

chunks.en: and it does not need the loaves.
chunks.st: And nevertheless the peace offering does not require the bringing of the loaves that accompany the peace offering of naziriteship, as it is written with regard to the loaves: “And shall place them on the hands of the nazirite” (Numbers 6:19), and in this case the nazirite is dead.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches that the blood of korbanos has no me'ilah at first but does at the end, while the wine offerings have me'ilah at first but not at the end.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: The blood is light at the start and strict at the end,
chunks.st: With regard to misuse of the blood of offerings that is to be sprinkled on the altar, the halakha is lenient with regard to the status of the blood at the outset and stringent at its conclusion.

chunks.en: and the wine offerings are strict at the start and light at the end.
chunks.st: With regard to misuse of the wine of the libations that accompany the offerings, the halakha is stringent with regard to the status of the wine at their outset and lenient at their conclusion.
chunks.stMore: The mishna explains:

words.note: Nesachim: wine poured on the mizbeach with korbanos.

chunks.en: The blood: at the start there is no me'ilah with it.
chunks.st: With regard to blood, at its outset, before it is sprinkled on the altar, one is not liable for misusing it;

chunks.en: Once it goes out to Nachal Kidron,
chunks.st: but once its remainder has been poured on the base of the altar and it emerges via the canal that runs through the Temple to the Kidron Valley
chunks.stMore: at the foot of the Temple Mount,

words.note: A valley next to the Har HaBayis, where the leftover blood flowed out.

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with it.
chunks.st: one is liable for misusing it.

chunks.en: The wine offerings: at the start there is me'ilah with them.
chunks.st: With regard to libations, at their outset, from the moment they were consecrated, one is liable for misusing them,

chunks.en: Once they go down into the shissin,
chunks.st: but once they have descended to the drainpipes
chunks.stMore: built into the altar and which extend beneath it, through which the libations flowed out of the Temple,

words.note: Pipes under the mizbeach that the wine flowed down into.

chunks.en: there is no me'ilah with them.
chunks.st: one is no longer liable for misusing them, as their mitzva was fulfilled and therefore their sanctity has ceased.

summary: Some things may not be used, but if someone did use them there is no me'ilah: the ashes from the inner mizbeach and the Menorah, and doves that are too young or too old for a korban. Rabbi Shimon disagrees about the young turtledoves.

chunks.en: The ashes cleared from the inner mizbeach and the Menorah,
chunks.st: With regard to the removal of ash from the inner altar to the place where the ashes lifted from the outer altar are deposited, and similarly with regard to the wicks of the Candelabrum,

words.note: The golden mizbeach inside the Heichal, for the ketores.

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit from them ab initio; but if one derived benefit from them he is not liable for their misuse.

chunks.en: Someone who makes the ashes hekdesh all over again,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates anew the ash that has been removed,

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with them.
chunks.st: he is liable for misusing it.

chunks.en: Turtledoves whose time has not yet come,
chunks.st: With regard to doves whose time of fitness for sacrifice has not arrived,
chunks.stMore: as they are too young,

words.note: Torim: a kind of dove brought as a korban when grown up.

chunks.en: and young pigeons whose time has passed,
chunks.st: and pigeons whose time of fitness for sacrifice has passed,
chunks.stMore: as they are too old,

words.note: Pigeons are brought as a korban only while young.

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit from them ab initio; but if one derived benefit from them he is not liable for their misuse.
chunks.stMore: The previous [mishna] teaches that one may not derive benefit from doves whose time of fitness for sacrifice has not arrived and from pigeons whose time of fitness for sacrifice has passed, but one who derived benefit from them is not liable for their misuse.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon disagrees with this ruling and says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: turtledoves whose time has not yet come,
chunks.st: With regard to doves whose time of fitness for sacrifice has not arrived,

chunks.en: have me'ilah.
chunks.st: one is liable for misusing them.

chunks.en: And young pigeons whose time has passed,
chunks.st: With regard to pigeons whose time of fitness for sacrifice has passed,

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit ab initio, but if one derived benefit from them he is not liable for their misuse.

summary: The milk of korban animals and the eggs of korban doves may not be used, but there is no me'ilah. That is only for things given to the mizbeach; for things given to fix the Beis HaMikdash, there is me'ilah with the eggs and milk too.

chunks.en: The milk of korban animals and the eggs of turtledoves
chunks.st: With regard to the milk of sacrificial animals and the eggs of sacrificial doves,

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit from them ab initio, but if one derived benefit from them after the fact he is not liable for their misuse.

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement, that if one derived benefit from the eggs or milk of sacrificial animals, he is not liable for their misuse, said?

chunks.en: With things given for the mizbeach.
chunks.st: It is stated in the case of sacrificial animals offered on the altar,
chunks.stMore: as their eggs and milk are not brought to the altar and therefore they are considered distinct from the offerings themselves.

chunks.en: But with things given for fixing the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: But this is not the halakha in the case of animals that are not sacrificed and are consecrated only for Temple maintenance.

words.note: Bedek HaBayis: things given for fixing and building the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: if he made a hen hekdesh,
chunks.st: For example, if one consecrated a hen

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with it and with its egg.
chunks.st: he is liable for misusing it and for misusing its egg;

chunks.en: A donkey: there is me'ilah with it and with its milk.
chunks.st: if one consecrated a donkey he is liable for misusing it and for misusing its milk, as the animal and its milk, and likewise the hen and its eggs, are both consecrated for Temple maintenance and are deemed a single unit.

summary: Anything made hekdesh has me'ilah, whether it is fit for the mizbeach, for fixing the Beis HaMikdash, or for neither. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Shimon argue about things that grew after it was made hekdesh, and the mishnah ends with animals, workers and cows near hekdesh food.

chunks.he: כָּל הָרָאוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְלֹא לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: Anything that is fit for the mizbeach and not for fixing the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: With regard to any consecrated item that is fit for sacrifice on the altar but is not fit for Temple maintenance,

chunks.en: for fixing the Beis HaMikdash and not for the mizbeach,
chunks.st: or if it is fit for Temple maintenance but not for sacrifice on the altar,

chunks.en: not for the mizbeach and not for fixing the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: or fit neither for the altar nor for Temple maintenance,

chunks.en: has me'ilah.
chunks.st: nevertheless one is liable for misusing it.
chunks.stMore: The mishna clarifies each of these categories: Fit for Temple maintenance but not for sacrifice on the altar,

chunks.en: How? If he made a pit full of water hekdesh,
chunks.st: how so? In a case where one consecrated a cistern full of water,
chunks.stMore: the water is not fit for sacrifice on the altar, as only water from the Siloam pool is used for the altar. Nevertheless, it is fit for Temple maintenance, e.g., to knead clay with it for use in reinforcing the walls of the Temple.

words.note: A bor: a hole dug to collect rainwater.

chunks.en: a garbage heap full of manure,
chunks.st: What is the case of an item fit neither for the altar nor for Temple maintenance? If one consecrated garbage dumps full of manure,
chunks.stMore: the place and its contents are fit neither for the altar nor for Temple maintenance. Rather, they are sold and the money received from the sale is donated to the Temple.

chunks.en: a dovecote full of doves,
chunks.st: What is the case of an item fit for sacrifice on the altar but not fit for Temple maintenance? If one consecrated a dovecote full of pigeons,
chunks.stMore: the pigeons are fit for the altar while the dovecote is not fit even for Temple maintenance.

words.note: A little house for doves.

chunks.en: a tree full of fruit,
chunks.st: Or if one consecrated a tree full of fruit,
chunks.stMore: as the fruit is fit for the altar whereas the tree is not fit even for Temple maintenance. For example, grapes are fit for the altar as wine, but the vines are not fit for Temple maintenance, as they are too flimsy for construction.

chunks.en: a field full of grass,
chunks.st: Another case where the consecrated item is fit for neither the altar nor Temple maintenance is a field full of grass.

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with them and with what is inside them.
chunks.st: In all those cases, one is liable for misusing both them and that which is within them,
chunks.stMore: as those that are unfit for use in the Temple will be sold and their money will be used for the altar or for Temple maintenance.

chunks.en: But if he made a pit hekdesh
chunks.st: But if one consecrated an empty cistern

chunks.en: and afterwards it filled up with water,
chunks.st: and it was subsequently filled with water,

chunks.en: a garbage heap and afterwards it filled up with manure,
chunks.st: or if one consecrated an empty garbage dump and it was subsequently filled with manure,

chunks.en: a dovecote and afterwards it filled up with doves,
chunks.st: or an empty dovecote and it was subsequently filled with pigeons,

chunks.en: a tree and afterwards it filled up with fruit,
chunks.st: or a tree without fruit and it was subsequently filled with fruit,

chunks.en: a field and afterwards it filled up with grass,
chunks.st: or an empty field and it was subsequently filled with grass;

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with them,
chunks.st: in all these cases one is liable for misusing them

chunks.en: but there is no me'ilah with what is inside them.
chunks.st: but one is not liable for misusing that which is within them.
chunks.stMore: There is no misuse with regard to enhancements that developed in consecrated property.

chunks.he: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehudah. But Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei disagrees in two of the above cases and says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a field or a tree hekdesh,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates the empty field in which grass grew or the empty tree
chunks.stMore: on which fruit grew,

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with them and with what grows on them,
chunks.st: he is liable for misusing both them and their growth,

words.en: and with what grows on them

chunks.en: because they are things that grew from hekdesh.
chunks.st: because these are growths of consecrated property,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that they grew there only after the property was consecrated.

chunks.he: וְלַד מְעֻשֶּׂרֶת לֹא יִינַק מִן הַמְעֻשֶּׂרֶת.
chunks.en: The baby of a maaser animal may not drink milk from the maaser animal.
chunks.st: Apropos the growths of consecrated property, the mishna states that an offspring born to a tithed animal before it was tithed may not be given to suckle from the tithed mother,
chunks.stMore: as it is a non-sacred animal that may not be allowed to derive benefit from consecrated property.

words.note: Every tenth animal is set aside as maaser and brought as a korban.

chunks.en: And some people give theirs on this condition.
chunks.explain: They make it hekdesh except for the milk.
chunks.st: And there are others who stipulate in this manner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., that the consecration does not apply to the milk.

chunks.he: וְלַד מֻקְדָּשִׁין לֹא יִינַק מִן הַמֻּקְדָּשִׁין.
chunks.en: The baby of korban animals may not drink milk from the korban animals.
chunks.st: The same is true of the offspring of sacrificial animals born to them before their consecration; they may not suckle from the sacrificial animal.

chunks.en: And some people give theirs on this condition.
chunks.st: And in this case as well, there are others who stipulate in this manner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., to enable the offspring to suckle.

chunks.he: הַפּוֹעֲלִים לֹא יֹאכְלוּ מִגְּרוֹגָרוֹת שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ.
chunks.en: The workers may not eat from dried figs of hekdesh.
chunks.st: The laborers, who are generally permitted to eat the food of their employer, may not eat from consecrated dried figs,
chunks.stMore: if they work with Temple produce. Rather, they can buy food with the money they are paid.

words.note: Hekdesh means set aside for the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: וְכֵן פָּרָה לֹא תֹאכַל מִכַּרְשִׁינֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ:
chunks.en: And so too a cow may not eat from vetch of hekdesh.
chunks.st: And likewise, a cow working with consecrated property, e.g., threshing Temple produce, may not eat from consecrated vetch [mikarshinei].

words.note: A plant used as animal food.

summary: Roots that grow between hekdesh land and an ordinary person's land, a spring in a hekdesh field, and the water of Sukkos in its golden jug may not be used, but there is no me'ilah. Once the water is put into the holy flask, there is me'ilah.

chunks.he: שָׁרְשֵׁי אִילָן שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט בָּאִין בְּשֶׁל
chunks.en: Roots of an ordinary person's tree that go into land of
chunks.st: With regard to the roots of the non-sacred tree of an ordinary person that enter into consecrated

chunks.he: הֶקְדֵּשׁ וְשֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ בָּאִין בְּשֶׁל הֶדְיוֹט,
chunks.en: hekdesh, or roots of hekdesh that go into an ordinary person's land,
chunks.st: land, and the roots of a consecrated tree that enter into the non-sacred land of an ordinary person,

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit from them ab initio, but if he derived benefit from them he is not liable for their misuse.

chunks.he: הַמַּעְיָן שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא מִתּוֹךְ שְׂדֵה הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
chunks.en: A spring that flows out through a field of hekdesh,
chunks.st: With regard to water of a spring that flows in a non-sacred field but which emerges from that field and flows into a consecrated field,

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: when it is in the consecrated field one may not derive benefit from it ab initio, but if one derived benefit from it he is not liable for its misuse.

chunks.en: Once it goes out of the field,
chunks.st: Once the spring emerges outside the consecrated field

chunks.en: one may use it.
chunks.st: one may derive benefit from the water.

chunks.en: The water in the golden jug
chunks.st: With regard to the water that was drawn from the Siloam pool into the golden jug,
chunks.stMore: which was not consecrated as a service vessel, to bring it to the altar for libation on the festival of Sukkot,

words.note: On Sukkos, water was poured on the mizbeach. It was carried in a golden jug.

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit from the water ab initio, as it was drawn for use in the Temple service. But if one derived benefit from it he is not liable for its misuse,
chunks.stMore: since it was not consecrated in a service vessel.

chunks.en: Once it is put into the flask,
chunks.st: Once one places the water from the jug for libation into the flask,
chunks.stMore: which is a service vessel, the water is consecrated and

words.note: A holy kli for pouring the water on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with it.
chunks.st: he is liable for misusing the water.

chunks.en: The aravah may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: With regard to the willow
chunks.stMore: branches that are placed on the sides of the altar on the festival of Sukkot, before their placement one may not derive benefit from them ab initio, but if he derived benefit from them he is not liable for their misuse. After their placement their mitzva has been fulfilled, and therefore at that time one may derive benefit from the willow branches ab initio.

words.note: Willow branches placed around the mizbeach on Sukkos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Tzadok says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:

chunks.en: the elders used to take from it for their lulavim.
chunks.st: The elders were accustomed to derive benefit from the willow branches even before their placement on the sides of the altar, by cutting small branches for use in their lulav, in fulfillment of the mitzva of the four species.

summary: A nest on top of a hekdesh tree may not be used, but there is no me'ilah. If someone makes a forest hekdesh, all of it has me'ilah, but wood bought by the treasurers has no me'ilah in its sawdust and leaves.

chunks.en: A nest on top of a hekdesh tree,
chunks.st: With regard to a bird’s nest that is atop the consecrated tree,

chunks.en: may not be used, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: one may not derive benefit from it ab initio, but if one derived benefit from it he is not liable for its misuse.

chunks.en: One that is on an asheirah, he knocks it down with a stick.
chunks.st: In order to acquire a bird’s nest that is atop a tree worshipped as idolatry, from which one may not derive benefit even by climbing it, one should dislodge the nest from its place by striking it with a pole.

words.note: A tree that people worshipped as avodah zarah.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a forest hekdesh,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates his forest,

chunks.en: all of it has me'ilah.
chunks.st: one is liable for misusing everything in the entire forest.

chunks.en: The treasurers who bought the wood,
chunks.st: In the case of the Temple treasurers who purchased non-sacred logs
chunks.stMore: to use for repairs in the Temple,

words.note: The people in charge of the money of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: there is me'ilah with the wood,
chunks.st: one is liable for misusing the wood itself,

chunks.he: וְאֵין מוֹעֲלִין לֹא בַשִּׁפּוּי וְלֹא בַנְּוִיָּה:
chunks.en: but no me'ilah with the sawdust or with the leaves.
chunks.st: but one is not liable for misusing the sawdust, nor is he liable for the leaves [baneviyya] that fall from the log, as the treasurers purchased for the Temple only those materials fit for use in its construction.
